sentences.text: The present first application under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed being aggrieved by the order dated 03.09.2015 passed by the Court of 4th Additional Sessions Judge, Guna, M.P. (Shri P.C. Gupta) in Criminal Revision No.77/2015, whereby the order dated 20.01.2015 passed by the Court of Judicial Magistrate, Guna (Shri A.K. Saxena), dismissing the unregistered complaint, has been affirmed.

sentences.text: 2. Briefly stated, the case of the complainant before the trial Court under Sections 406 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code was that in the year 2008, the accused persons, on the pretext of requiring money for the medical treatment of their grandfather (late Rameshwar Sharma), demanded a sum of Rs.5,000/- from the complainant.
Being acquainted with them, the complainant gave the said amount of Rs. 5,000/-.
Subsequently, on 27.08.2008, the grandfather of accused Jagdish passed away.
Said Rameshwar had executed a will bequeathing his land in favour of accused NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20792 2 MCRC-12281-2015 Jagdish.

Relying on the said will, the accused represented to the complainant that the land situated at Village Behanta Jhir, P.H. No. 80,
Survey No. 5/3, measuring 1.254 hectares, would be sold to him for a total consideration of Rs.1,65,000/-.

It was further stated that a sum of Rs.95,000/- was urgently required for performing the funeral rites and post-death ceremonies (terai, etc.) of their grandfather, and including the previously advanced Rs.5,000/-, the total payment would amount to Rs.1,00,000/-, with the balance of Rs.65,000/- being payable at the time of registration of the sale deed.

Believing the representations of the accused, the complainant handed over a sum of Rs.95,000/- on 01.09.2008,
whereupon accused Jagdish Sharma executed an agreement to sell in favour of the complainant with Neeraj Singh vs Jagdish Prasad on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143759851/
1 respect to the aforesaid land bequeathed under the will.

3. It is further stated in the complaint that despite the passage of considerable time and repeated requests by the complainant, the accused persons did not execute the registered sale deed of the aforesaid land in favour of the complainant.
Thereafter, the accused persons fraudulently executed a registered sale deed of the said land in favour of some other person, thereby deriving wrongful gain for themselves.

By first assuring the complainant that the land would be sold to him, accepting an advance sum of Rs.1,00,000/-, and executing an agreement to sell, but thereafter failing to convey the land to him, the accused persons committed criminal breach of trust.

4. The applicant further averred that for redressal of the said grievance, he submitted a written application to Police Station Cantt., but no action was NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:20792 3 MCRC-12281-2015 taken by the police.

It is alleged that the accused persons, with the intention of cheating, induced the complainant by assuring the sale of the land,
received Rs.1,00,000/- as advance consideration, executed an agreement to sell, but subsequently sold the land to another person, thereby deceiving the complainant.
Hence, praying that appropriate penal action be taken against the accused persons for having committed the acts of cheating and criminal breach of trust, a complaint was made before the trial Court.
The trial Court, upon recording preliminary evidence under Sections 200 and 202 Cr.P.C., vide order dated 20.01.2015 dismissed the complaint holding that no prima facie case was made out.
The revisional Court, vide order dated 03.09.2015, affirmed the said finding.
Assailing both the orders, the present petition has been filed.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner has urged that the Courts below erred in dismissing the complaint at the threshold.

It is contended that despite receiving advance consideration and executing an agreement to sell, the accused failed to honour their commitment and dishonestly sold the property elsewhere, which clearly establishes deceit.

It is further contended that at the stage of cognizance, the Court ought to have examined only whether the complaint disclosed essential ingredients of the alleged offences, and not whether the material was sufficient to secure conviction.

Thus, it is prayed that present petition be allowed and both the impugned orders be set-aside.
6.
Having considered the submissions and perused the record, it is evident that the dispute essentially arises out of a contractual transaction in respect of an agreement to sell immovable property.

The allegations, even if NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20792 4 MCRC-12281-2015 taken at their face value, disclose that the grievance of the petitioner is that despite execution of the agreement to sell and receipt of advance consideration, the non-applicants did not execute the sale deed and alienated the property elsewhere.

Such grievance squarely falls within the realm of civil dispute and the appropriate remedy available to the petitioner is to institute a civil suit seeking specific performance of an agreement or other appropriate relief.
7.
At the stage of taking cognizance, the trial Court rightly considered that the complaint did not disclose the necessary ingredients of the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 IPC.

Mere breach of contract or failure to perform an agreement, in the absence of dishonest or fraudulent intention at the inception of the transaction, does not constitute a criminal offence of cheating or Neeraj Singh vs Jagdish Prasad on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143759851/
2 criminal breach of trust.
8.

Consequently, this Court is of the opinion that the orders passed by the trial Court as well as revisional court do not suffer from any illegality or perversity warranting interference under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
9.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, the petition fails and is hereby dismissed.

It is, however,
observed that the petitioner shall be at liberty to avail appropriate civil remedy by filing a suit for specific performance of agreement or any other relief as may be permissible in law.
